subject: Intermittent controller auth failures on Novum Health private deployment — trace request & SLA question
messages:
From: Dana Patel <dana.patel@novumhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent auth failures after minor agent upgrade (Novum-prod)

Hi Sofia,

We started seeing intermittent control-plane auth failures against our private deployment after the agent patch that shipped last night (agent v1.2.0 -> v1.2.1). Symptoms: brief 30-120s windows where inference requests fail with 401-like control RPC auth errors, and the agent restarts sometimes report token refresh failures. This impacted three customer-facing services between 02:40-03:15 UTC and again briefly at 06:07 UTC.

Can you please:
- Pull a full trace around 2026-04-22T02:40:00Z — 03:20:00Z and 2026-04-22T06:05:00Z — 06:15:00Z
- Provide any evidence packages we can use for our audit (logs, event traces, install diffs)
- Confirm whether this meets the SLA incident criteria and whether we should expect a credit (we'll need the basis for our procurement team)

We can provision a short bridge if helpful — we'll also consider rolling the agents back if that's safer.

Attaching a cropped agent stderr excerpt showing the token error (privnet-sample-stderr.txt).

Thanks,
Dana
Senior SRE
Novum Health

Dana — thanks for the quick heads up and the stderr excerpt. Sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as a high-priority escalation.

Next steps from our side (short term):
- I'm scheduling a 30m bridge in 30 minutes to collect live traces if the issue recurs. Invite will follow.
- Jonas & Marcus are pulling control-plane and agent telemetry now; we'll deliver an evidence bundle covering the two windows you listed.
- If you are open, rolling back the agent to v1.2.0 is an acceptable temporary mitigation; we can coordinate a targeted rollback for the services you nominate.

For the SLA question: we'll collect the evidence and correlate against our incident credit policy and get back within 24h. If you need a formal request routed to contracts, include contracts@novumhealth.com and we'll CC them on the credit analysis.

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Dana Patel <dana.patel@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Novum Health Contracts <contracts@novumhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent auth failures after minor agent upgrade (Novum-prod)

Dana — follow-up with the evidence bundle and immediate remediation status. Thanks for the pod IDs; they made matching traces straightforward.

What we did:
- Rollback: We coordinated a targeted rollback of the agent on the three pods you listed at 2026-04-22T15:12:00Z. That mitigated the short windows of 401-like failures.
- Evidence bundle (attached): privnet-trace-20260422.log (control-plane/agent correlation), kube-events-20260422.json, and a short diagnostic summary. The bundle contains the timestamped RPC failures and the token refresh loop observed on agents.
- Fix deployed: engineering shipped v1.2.1-rc2 (hotfix) to address a token-refresh sequencing race that could occur during rolling upgrades; the fix prevents stale token reuse when the local sequencer restarts. Hotfix applied to your fleet at 2026-04-23T03:10:00Z.

Preliminary root cause (short): a race between agent-side token refresh and the control-plane's short-lived token rotation under specific restart timing during a rolling patch. We have an open task to make token refresh idempotent and to add an extra recovery path so a single refresh failure won't cascade to restarts.

SLA credit: based on the impact windows and our credit policy, we estimate this qualifies for a partial credit. We're proposing a 5% credit on April invoice as a good-faith remediation while we finalize the postmortem. If that works, please confirm and we will route the credit approval to finance and CC contracts@novumhealth.com.

Next deliverables we will provide by EOD:
- Completed postmortem PDF with timeline, root cause analysis, and mitigations (attached as draft).
- JIRA link to the remediation epic: https://rwd.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-3321
- Permanent mitigation ETA: two weeks for the idempotent refresh change and one-month runway for additional hardening and increased telemetry.

If you'd like a short exec-level summary for your procurement packet, I can prepare that as well.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Dana Patel <dana.patel@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent auth failures after minor agent upgrade (Novum-prod)

Adding a technical closure note for the record. We've completed the postmortem draft attached and the remediation tickets are queued:
- Root cause: token refresh sequencer did not guard against partially-applied state during concurrent restarts; under specific timing the agent would attempt a refresh with a stale nonce and trigger an auth-fail loop.
- Short-term mitigation: rollback + hotfix (v1.2.1-rc2) deployed; added a 10s randomized backoff before sequencer retry to reduce collision probability.
- Long-term: idempotent refresh path + stronger telemetry (per-agent sequence numbers, trace ids) and a canary rollout policy tweak for rolling upgrades.

Action items:
- RINF-3321: implement idempotent refresh (owner: Priyom — ETA 2026-05-06)
- RINF-3330: add per-agent seq telemetry and sampling (owner: Marcus — ETA 2026-05-13)
- Ops playbook update to include signaled rollback path for rolling upgrades (owner: Jonas — ETA 2026-05-03)

I'll sync with finance on the 5% credit flow once Sofia confirms. Thanks everyone for the rapid collaboration.

-Marcus
Engineering Manager, Runtime
